description:
Profile and optimize mid-range logical buffer operations on the Ryzen 9 5900X, retaining the requirement that adoption materially improves real workloads.

## Background

Buffers of 8-64 words can be dominated by dispatch and call overhead as well as instruction throughput. The relevant production consumers are row operations, parity generation and dense matrix work. Measure actual consumers before selecting unrolling, zero-copy access, fusion or memory-traffic changes; do not infer performance from the AVX2 label.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Publish profiles and baseline measurements for 8-64-word logical operations and their production consumers, with neighboring smaller/larger sizes and boundary/unaligned cases. Freeze exact operations, inputs, cache regimes, statistical rules and primary consumer cells before optimization.

- [hard] REQ-02: Compare candidate unroll factors, dispatch hoisting, zero-copy BitSlice use and measured useful fusions against the established kernels. Adopt an optimization only when the protocol's confidence-bound rule demonstrates greater than 15% speedup on its declared real-workload cells and the frozen non-regression rule passes elsewhere. Preserve a measured no-win outcome if none qualifies.

- [hard] REQ-03: Compare equivalent XOR/parity operations against ISA-L and consuming dense-matrix work against M4RI. Match input representation and operation semantics and include all adapter, setup, conversion and output costs; distinguish isolated throughput from consumer benefit.

- [hard] REQ-04: Preserve exact logical semantics, canonical bit indexing and zero tail padding in the shared suites. Keep the one canonical buffer/dispatch abstraction and route measured decisions through existing tuning mechanisms.

- [hard] REQ-05: Commit annotated release assembly and profiles explaining dispatch overhead, memory traffic, spills, dependence limits or bandwidth saturation. Produce reviewed worker-sized implementation leaves if the measured story needs several independent changes.

- [hard] REQ-06: Pass the shared behavioral and external conformance suites for every affected implementation, preserve the declared numerical contract and deterministic seeded execution, and exercise scalar fallback plus relevant empty, unaligned, partial-batch, and 0/1/63/64/65 bit-boundary cases. Compile intrinsic-bearing designs with Rust 1.95 before implementation decomposition; verify the shipped code at that MSRV.

- [hard] REQ-07: Publish committed before/after and matching open-source comparison receipts, with machine-readable samples and a Markdown interpretation, under the issue's configured dev/bench_results directory. Record exact commands, source and comparator revisions, input identities and seeds, compiler flags, runtime-selected paths, and runtime-observed hardware provenance. Register external sources in the citation registry and link durable artifacts at their final paths.

- [hard] REQ-08: Measure optimized release/bench builds on the Ryzen 9 5900X under the existing exclusive benchmark lock on a verified quiet host. Finish builds before measurement, record affinity, clocks/governor and SMT state, and use bounded resumable runs with an append-only execution log opened and printed before the first run.

- [hard] REQ-09: Freeze workloads, sample/repetition budgets, warmup, confidence level, improvement and per-cell non-regression tolerances, material-gap threshold, and stopping rules in a versioned premeasurement protocol before optimization trials. Cover small inputs, crossover regions, cache-resident and streaming sizes, kernel-only costs, setup/conversion costs, and representative production consumers; record inapplicable cells explicitly.

- [hard] REQ-10: Adopt production candidates only when the predeclared confidence-bound improvement and non-regression rules pass on their intended dispatch domain. Preserve all negative and inconclusive outcomes; retain the established implementation where no candidate qualifies. Report ratios to the fastest compatible measured external arm, without pooling incompatible operations or concealing losing cells in an aggregate.

- [hard] REQ-11: Explain outcomes with committed assembly and profiler evidence for instruction mix, dependencies, spills, allocation, cache traffic, or bandwidth limits. Preserve architecture boundaries and canonical abstractions, keep unsafe code in isolated kernels, and publish a ranked explanation and tracked disposition for every material residual gap. A documented no-win result is acceptable; an unexplained skipped comparison is not.

## Notes

The greater-than-15% real-workload adoption requirement is retained from this story's scope. It is stricter than the generic confidence-bound improvement rule and is not a global requirement on other CPU optimization work. No implementation changes are part of issue creation.
title: Profile and optimize mid-range buffer operations (8-64 words)
